title: Measurements flow into the quote
why: No retyping a measurement report into a proposal.
today: Roofr's own reports feed proposals directly
Third-party reports like GAF QuickMeasure can't be imported; area and edge lengths are typed in by hand
salesforce: QuickMeasure provides PDF, XML and DXF files
Strong CRM parses the XML: area, pitch, ridges, hips, valleys, eaves, rakes and flashing
The report arrives by email to Salesforce, or a rep uploads it, and quote lines build automatically
cost: 20 hours, replacing the Roofr integration line in the SOW (no net change)

note.text: GAF doesn't publish its XML layout, so Strong CRM will test the parser on one of your real reports.

title: Waste per line item, adjusted for pitch and complexity
why: Different waste for shingles, underlayment, ridge cap and the rest, not one blanket %.
today: Each catalog item has a default waste %
Proposals have a waste column on every line, and the report's recommended waste can be applied to it
No documented rules for adjusting waste by pitch or complexity
salesforce: Each product carries a default waste % and a coverage per unit
Reps can override the waste % on any line
A complexity rule adds waste on steep or cut-up roofs; QuickMeasure's suggested waste can pre-fill the lines
Quantities round up to whole bundles, rolls and pieces
cost: Fields and a Flow in the base build

note.text: The waste worksheet below works the way the quote does. The same six lines run in our demo org, where a Flow sets each line's waste % and order quantity. Confirming: Strong CRM's hours for this.

title: A proposal that looks like Cannon
why: Branding, job photos, good/better/best options, clean line items.
today: Unlimited templates with cover pages, logo, photos (including CompanyCam), PDFs and text pages
Several options for the homeowner to choose from, plus upgrades
Line items can be hidden from the homeowner and still count in totals
salesforce: Standard quote templates cover logo, layout, line items, pricing and a signature block
Standard templates don't handle job-specific photos or sections that change by option
For those: Salesforce Document Generation (templates built in Word with images and conditional sections), or Strong CRM's Advanced PDFs
cost: Included, or the Advanced PDFs add-on

note.text: Whether Document Generation is included with your licenses, which would make Advanced PDFs unnecessary, and how many photos fit on a page.

title: Know when a homeowner opens the proposal
why: Open and view notifications so reps follow up at the right moment.
today: "Viewed" status when the homeowner opens it (added June 2026)
Time-stamped status history on the job card
Click or time-on-page tracking isn't documented
salesforce: The e-signature tool writes sent, viewed and signed statuses back to the opportunity
A Flow alerts the rep the moment a proposal is viewed
Salesforce email open tracking can also be turned on

title: E-signature
why: Sign on the spot or from a link, without extra friction.
today: Built in, with unlimited signatures on Essentials and Scale at no extra charge
Sign on the device or by email or text link
salesforce: Option A: DocuSign eSignature for Salesforce (listed from $30 per user per month)
Option B: Appiphony eSign Connect ($12 per user per month, billed annually), which still needs a DocuSign account
Option C: on-site signature in the Field Service mobile app, using licenses you already have (to be confirmed for quotes)
cost: New compared with Roofr; depends on how many people send proposals

note.text: The all-in yearly cost of each option for your sending volume.

title: QuickBooks
why: Signed jobs become invoices without re-keying.
today: QuickBooks Online sync is a beta, on the Scale plan only
One-way, exported by hand, one company file
salesforce: Strong CRM connects QuickBooks directly or through Zapier
Customers, jobs and invoices stay in sync with the opportunity

note.text: QuickBooks Online or Desktop, and what triggers an invoice (deposit, milestone or completion).
